analysis.title: Global Reflections (Louis Miller, FICC & Equities), 30 Oct 2026
key_insights: Markets sold off into Halloween and the AI pain trade continued. Hyperscaler earnings left investors focused on AI funding and returns. Appetite to add risk outside AI is weak ahead of the midterms and a decision on Iran.

Demand for trades uncorrelated to AI and oil is described as the highest it has been. GS sees the best opportunities in pockets of Healthcare. The broadening trade (SPXXAI) worked in October, but a weaker growth outlook calls for caution on pockets that mainly benefited from a short squeeze.

In a Democratic sweep at the midterms, GS's favorite long is the Affordable Care Act Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA). Democrats are pushing to revive the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that expired at end-2025. Reauthorization should help hospitals, outpatient providers and health insurers that face rising bad debt and uncompensated care costs.

A Democratic sweep scenario also favors AI Power (GSENEPOW) if more power supply is framed as the fix for electricity inflation. Policymaker convergence on datacenter cost bearing could weaken datacenter project economics and weigh on the ex-Power AI hardware trade (GSTMTAIH).

Corporate tax (GSPUTAXP) is flagged as a topic to watch. Because the President can veto legislation, midterms are unlikely to change tax law, so 2027-28 earnings are largely insulated. A higher tax rate further out implies risk to earnings and valuations beyond 2029.

GS revamped its Healthcare AI Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCAIP) to cover diagnostics, genomic and biological data, laboratory automation and precision medicine. Many constituents have reported productivity and commercial proof points. The basket has outperformed the broader Healthcare sector (S5HLTH) YTD and shows low correlation to AI, rates and oil.

The Systematic Trading Strategy team's Growth Value Rotator is another uncorrelated trade, with the long-only GSRHBUBG +27% YTD and the long/short GSRHBUBT +18%. It is meant to capture Growth/Value rotations without calling their timing or direction.

Software versus Semis (GSPUSOSE) is +88% from June lows, partly from the reversal of momentum and partly because the Software AI disruption narrative has become more nuanced. Software forward P/E rose from 17x to 23x in four months, and Software is much less exposed to short momentum than on January 1. Earnings should show where structural pressure exists and where moats hold.

GS sees Insurance (GSXUINSU, GSXEINSU) as a pocket of underpriced AI disruption. Crypto cyber-attack headlines point to underappreciated underwriting risk. The sector had a defensive rally in October, and broader risk relief could rotate Financials flow back to banks.

GS expects the global cybersecurity addressable market to keep growing as AI use cases expand. Leading cybersecurity companies are concentrated in the US (GSTMTCYB), and clients are showing more interest in global expressions of the theme.

European Banks had their worst month since March 2023. GS does not expect significant OAT-Bund tightening near term, but sees the underperformance as overdone given limited spillover risk to a wider regional sovereign crisis and solid fundamentals (+200bp ROTE expansion to 2028E).

GS likes buying Greek Banks (GSXEGRBK) after a 10% de-rating. Supports are 3Q NII beats versus consensus, the Alpha Bank capital markets day on Nov 5 and MSCI's developed market upgrade in May 2027 as a runway for institutional inflows.

Japanese Banks (GSXAJMEB) have disconnected from solid earnings. BoJ signaling of a December hike sets the group up for a year-end relief rally. The stated risk is that an 'escalate to de-escalate' strategy does not materialize, which would add inflation and rates pain.

European Defense (GSSBDEFE) is up 13% over three weeks, helped by its non-AI exposure and high short crowding. GS research expects European defense spend to grow at an 8% CAGR over FY25-30E, while valuations imply declining medium-term earnings. GS expects 3Q results and strategy updates to show progress on production ramps, earnings growth and cash generation.
If the market again prices positive medium-term earnings growth for European Defense, GS sees potential for a c.30% re-rating back to September 2025 valuation levels.
